channel.title: The Brussels Times
channel.description: Latest posts from The Brussels Times.

item.title: Thousands take to streets ahead of crucial German elections
item.description: Thousands protested for democracy on the streets of Magdeburg ahead of tomorrow's statewide elections, where the far-right AfD party is a clear frontrunner.

item.title: Moscow bombs Kyiv airport ahead of American visit
item.description: The details of the damage are still unknown. Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff, two US envoys, are travelling to Ukraine this weekend.

item.title: Over 1,000 Europeans infected by West Nile virus
item.description: Most of the cases so far have been identified in Southern and Western European countries. The virus is spread mainly through mosquito bites.

item.title: Trump wants Europe to pay for aid granted to Ukraine by Biden
item.description: Donald Trump says he will ask European countries to pay the United States for aid given to Ukraine under former President Joe Biden.

item.title: Glorifying Mladic is a crime, Council of Europe warns
item.description: The Council of Europe warns that the “glorification” of late former Bosnian Serb military chief Ratko Mladic, is a crime under Bosnian law.

item.title: Belgium and India to significantly strengthen military cooperation
item.description: “No statements without commitment, but joint training, industrial projects and opportunities for our companies,” Belgian defence minister stated.

item.title: Zelenskyy furious after Ukrainian spy agencies' friendly fire shootout in central Kyiv
item.description: A spy-drama-style shootout happened in broad daylight in central Kyiv due to misunderstanding between two security forces.

item.title: Extreme heat weather events expected to rise further through 2027 due to El Niño
item.description: “We are already seeing the disruption and devastation caused by droughts and floods, and we expect these effects to worsen"

item.title: Norway detains Russian ship ordered to compensate Ukrainian energy agency
item.description: Norway seizes Russian vessel in connection with a court ruling ordering Russia to pay about $4.22 billion in compensation to Ukrainian energy agency Naftogaz.

item.title: European Commission does not confirm Spanish Prime Minister’s allegations about Ceuta
item.description: “We have no conclusive evidence to suggest that the crisis was triggered by disinformation from foreign state actors.”

item.title: New series of suspected sabotage acts carried out against German critical infrastructure
item.description: Explosives have been found at the site of a Belgian-owned electrical substation in the eastern German state of Brandenburg.

item.title: Ryanair cuts winter flights and warns of price hikes due to high fuel prices
item.description: Due to reduced winter schedule, Ryanair expects no passenger growth this winter compared to a year earlier.

item.title: Zelenskyy wants to block Russian sky: 'We are warning our partners – days of safety are over'
item.description: Ukraine will, however, respond favourably to requests from its partners not to disrupt flights to Russia “at specific times".

item.title: UN warns world is exceeding dangerous limit of 1.5 degrees for global warming
item.description: This does not mean that the long-term goal of limiting warming to 1.5°C by the end of the century is lost.

item.title: Red Crescent reports 4 deaths at a wedding in US airstrike in Iran
item.description: Four people, including a child, were killed and over 50 injured in a US attack that struck a wedding house in Iran, the Iranian Red Crescent says.

item.title: European gas prices at their highest level since early 2023
item.description: European gas prices top €74 per megawatt hour (MWh), their highest level since early 2023, as renewed escalation in the Middle East pushes up energy markets.

item.title: Belgian biopharma group reaches agreement with US to reduce medication prices
item.description: The agreement specifically pertains to medicines for Medicaid, the public health insurance programme, which helps cover medical expenses for low-income households.

item.title: US Army Secretary Dan Driscoll resigns
item.description: US Army Secretary Dan Driscoll has resigned after months of tensions with Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth, the White House confirmed on Monday.

item.title: Former French P.M. Edouard Balladur dies at the age of 97
item.description: Former French Prime Minister Edouard Balladur has died in Paris at the age of 97, his family told French news agency AFP on Monday.

item.title: Brigitte Bardot's belongings to be auctioned in Paris
item.description: Auction house Millon announces that 285 everyday items once owned by Bardot will go under the hammer in Paris on 21 September.
